title: Concurrent Opioid Use and the Overturn Ceiling for Acute Migraine Drugs
content:
For the authorization owed after an overturned quantity limit denial on an acute migraine drug under the Utilization Management Program, concurrent opioid use changes how the overturn ceiling is worked out from the drug's limit times the multiple applied to it.

**Rule.** When the member's paid oxycodone-acetaminophen retail fills dated within the last three months add up to 30 or more days supply, one unit for each average monthly opioid day (those days supply divided by 3) is subtracted, a day of opioid treatment displacing one acute migraine dose; when they add up to between 1 and 29 days supply, the limit times the multiple is multiplied by 0.9; when there is no such fill, it is used as it stands.

The fills are paid retail claims under the Retail Pharmacy Network Benefit. The three months end on the date the authorization is put in force: a fill counts when dated after the same day of the month three months before that date. The days supply of every such fill is totalled. The resulting figure is not rounded here; the overturn ceiling is rounded down to a whole unit only at the end.

## Input, judgement, result (hypothetical: limit times the multiple is 18)

| Total opioid days supply | Judgement | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | no such fill | 18 |
| 10 | between 1 and 29 | 18 multiplied by 0.9: 16.2 |
| 29 | between 1 and 29 | 16.2 |
| 30 | 30 or more | 18 less 10: 8 |
| 45 | 30 or more | 18 less 15: 3 |
